question: Should OpenClaw core own ClawHub publisher-feed retrieval and its signing trust roots, or should this protocol remain in a plugin/ClawHub-owned integration behind a generic core seam?
rationale: The branch introduces a new signed remote-content trust boundary in core, but no production caller currently establishes who controls publisher endpoints, trusted keys, lifecycle, or failure policy.

options.title: Pause and define ownership
options.body: Hold this stacked series until the core-versus-plugin owner and trust-root lifecycle are explicitly approved and documented.

options.title: Approve core ownership
options.body: Keep the implementation in core, but add the approved configuration owner, production caller, upgrade behavior, and end-to-end trust proof before merge.

options.title: Move behind plugin seam
options.body: Keep ClawHub-specific protocol and policy outside core, adding only a generic extension API if existing plugin surfaces are insufficient.

recommendation.title: Pause and define ownership
recommendation.body: Hold this stacked series until the core-versus-plugin owner and trust-root lifecycle are explicitly approved and documented.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is repeated ownership of the guarded network and SSRF boundary used by this feature.
